outcome: Control verbs stop holding the run hostage: Start, AnswerAttention, and Control return once the command is durable while the drive continues under a background owner in the same process lifetime or a named resumable state - so a closed laptop lid, a piped answer, or a timeout wrapper can never again orphan a run mid-dispatch.

exclude: journal schema or control-gate changes (owner lease semantics are unchanged; existing journals stay valid)
a system daemon or service manager (in-process background ownership plus the existing resume path only)
changing what any verb is permitted to do (only when it returns)

acceptance.text: sworn answer returns success once the answer is durably recorded, with the drive continuing: pinned by a runtime fixture asserting the verb returns while the run subsequently reaches its next effect, and that killing the caller after return does not orphan the run into a claimed-unexpired state.
sworn run offers a detached mode where the command returns after the run is claimed and driving, printing where to watch it; the foreground mode remains: pinned by cmd/sworn fixtures over both modes.
Resume and takeover return once ownership transition is durable, and their status output names the run's live state rather than blocking until completion: pinned by runtime control fixtures.
The real-binary lifecycle scenario proves detach: start detached, answer from a second process, observe completion - declared as CI evidence in test/e2e (ADR 0010), not executed by any role.

constraints: Exactly one owner drives at a time; the lease model is untouched - this slice changes who waits, never who owns.
A durable-then-die failure between record and drive must land in an already-recoverable state (the existing resume path), never a new wedge class.

Evidence basis: AnswerAttention and Control end in driveOwned on the caller's goroutine (internal/runtime/service.go:1083-1100, :1151, :1176); a piped answer orphaned a run twice in one night (sworn#192); the TUI freezes because Start drives its foreground (cmd/sworn/tui_backend.go:506).
The e2e check is declared, not executed by a role (ADR 0010).
Check evidence belongs in the submission's checks field, never in files added to the repository.
